# A click's event data omits the pointer type that produced it

## Context

The web desktop (#21075, PR #21087) opens an app on a single tap on a touch device, while a mouse click only selects and a double-click opens. Emmy's review of #21087 (Request Changes, `5914795110`) showed that on a touch-capable computer a mouse click opens the app too. The launcher can only consult the device flag (`Neo.config.hasTouchEvents`), because the click that reaches the app worker does not say which pointer produced it. In her Chromium probe the native click events did carry it: `pointerType: "mouse"` for a trusted mouse click and `"touch"` for a finger tap, in one context.

## The Problem

An app that answers a tap differently from a click has no per-event signal to read, so it either guesses from the device or treats every input alike. The guess is wrong on every hybrid device: a laptop with a touch screen, a tablet with a mouse or a pen.

## The Architectural Reality

- `Neo.main.DomEvents#onClick`, `onDoubleClick`, `onContextMenu` and the other mouse handlers serialize the event through `getMouseEventData` (`src/main/DomEvents.mjs`). That method copies a fixed list of `MouseEvent` fields (`altKey`, `button`, `buttons`, `clientX` … `shiftKey`) and nothing else.
- In current Chromium, `click`, `auxclick` and `contextmenu` are `PointerEvent`s carrying `pointerType` (`"mouse"`, `"pen"`, `"touch"`). `dblclick`, `mousedown` and `mouseup` are plain `MouseEvent`s without it. A browser that dispatches `click` as a `MouseEvent` carries none either.
- The drag sensors read `pointerType` on the main thread (`src/main/draggable/sensor/Pointer.mjs`, #17889), but nothing forwards it to the app worker.

## The Fix

- `getMouseEventData` copies `pointerType` with the other fields: the event's value where it has one, and `undefined` where it has none, so an app can tell "no signal" from "mouse".
- Its JSDoc names the field and the fallback a consumer needs.
- A unit arm in `test/playwright/unit/main/DomEvents.spec.mjs` proves both: a click carrying `pointerType: "touch"` reaches the app with it, and a double-click without one reaches it with `undefined`.

## Contract Ledger Matrix

| Target Surface | Source of Authority | Proposed Behavior | Fallback | Docs | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Mouse event data sent to the app worker (`Neo.main.DomEvents#getMouseEventData`) | the native event | adds `pointerType`, copied from the event | `undefined` when the event carries none (`MouseEvent`, older browsers) | the method's JSDoc | the unit arm; #21087's launcher reading it |

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1 a click whose native event carries `pointerType` reaches the app worker with the same value.
- [ ] AC-2 a mouse event without one (a `dblclick`, a `MouseEvent` click) reaches it with `pointerType: undefined`; every other field is unchanged.
- [ ] AC-3 the JSDoc of `getMouseEventData` names the field and its fallback.

## Out of Scope

- Forwarding `pointerdown` / `pointerup` as their own app events.
- Changing the drag sensors.
- Any consumer change. The web desktop launcher reads the field in #21087, which carries this change.

## Avoided Traps

- Inferring the pointer from the device (`Neo.config.hasTouchEvents`): it is constant per device, while hybrid devices switch per event.
- Correlating a separately forwarded `pointerdown` with the next click in the app: two messages, an ordering assumption and state in every consumer, for a field the click already has.
